clue.text: Leader of players, strong and fit, left out — pitiful

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so take the opening letter of players
left out means the letter for left is removed from the synonym for strong and fit

parts.note: an athletic person is strong and fit

explanation.surface: A team captain, strong and fit, is dropped from the side, which is a sorry state of affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of' gives P; 'out' removes L from ATHLETIC, leaving ATHETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something so feeble or sad that it arouses pity or contempt.

clue.text: River rising in southern part of 19

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
in a down entry the southern part is the lower end, so the top letters are dropped and the tail kept

parts.note: the answer to 19 down is the European peninsula of Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: A river flows up out of the south of the Spanish peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'southern part of' keeps ERIA, the bottom of IBERIA in its down light; 'rising' turns it to read upwards. The AIRE is a river in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aire is a Yorkshire waterway flowing through Leeds, so it is a named example of a river.

clue.text: Architect offers for sale house partly put up

parts.note: to hawk goods is to peddle them, so someone who offers for sale hawks

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a room is one part of a house

explanation.surface: An architect hawks a house that has been half built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns ROOM into MOOR. Nicholas Hawksmoor was the English Baroque architect of several London churches.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas Hawksmoor was a celebrated English Baroque designer of churches, an example of the profession named.

clue.text: Bentham mostly translated ancient Egyptian or Greek

indicators.note: translated suggests the letters are rendered into a new form, so they are rearranged
mostly means all but the final letter of the name is used

parts.note: Jeremy Bentham, the philosopher, taken as written

explanation.surface: A philosopher's work, mostly translated, concerns the ancient world of Egypt or Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims BENTHAM to BENTHA, and 'translated' rearranges those letters. There was a Thebes in Egypt and another in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a city both on the Nile and in Boeotia, so a native of either was so called.

clue.text: One's set daily offering light entertainment

definitions.text: One's set daily offering light entertainment

parts.words: One's set daily offering light entertainment
parts.note: read as a newspaper feature compiled each day, made of lights (grid entries), giving gentle amusement

explanation.surface: Something devised every day offers easy-going fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like 'not heavy', but it is also the crossword word for an entry in the grid; 'set' is what a setter does.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily newspaper puzzle is set by a compiler, filled with lights, and enjoyed as a diversion.

clue.text: Abdicate from kingship, installing son

indicators.note: installing means the son is placed inside the word for kingship

parts.note: a reign is a monarch's period of kingship

explanation.surface: A monarch gives up the crown, putting his son on the throne instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to give up an office, especially a throne, formally.

clue.text: In oil works, extremely rare to have elaborate decoration

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word rare, its first and last letters

parts.note: finery is showy, elaborate clothing or ornament

explanation.surface: Oil paintings rarely have ornate decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives RE, the first and last letters of 'rare'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant where crude petroleum is processed is an industrial works for oil.

clue.text: Cancel contribution, although receiving credit

indicators.note: receiving means the word for contribution takes the credit abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a sub is a subscription, a regular contribution to a club

explanation.surface: Someone cancels a donation even though it is earning credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'although' is only a link here; a sub is short for a subscription paid to a club.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is informal for calling it off.

clue.text: Take ultimate risk after attack went wrong

parts.note: to go for someone is to attack them
a machine that broke went wrong

explanation.surface: After an assault fails, someone gambles everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means staking everything on one bold attempt, the greatest gamble possible.

clue.text: Medical author put off and fed up

parts.note: Sir Thomas Browne wrote Religio Medici, so he is the author of the Medici, or a medical author
to doff a hat is to take it off

explanation.surface: A doctor who writes takes off his clothes and is fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Thomas Browne was a seventeenth-century physician and author of Religio Medici. BROWNED OFF is British slang for fed up.
explanation.definitionFit: The British slang phrase means bored and annoyed, the same as being weary of something.

clue.text: Fine skin rejected for fancy collar

indicators.note: rejected means the word for skin is sent back, so read it backwards

parts.note: fur is an animal's hairy skin
F is the standard abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A fine animal skin is turned down in favour of a decorative collar.
explanation.definitionFit: An Elizabethan pleated neckpiece, stiff and frilled, is a showy collar.

clue.text: It was standard to highlight ship ping hazards

parts.note: the star of a show is its highlight
sandbars are banks of sand that ground passing vessels

explanation.surface: It used to be normal to mark the dangers to vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: The page splits 'shipping' across a line. The Stars and Bars was the first flag of the American Confederacy, and a flag is a standard.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag carried in battle is a standard, and this was the Confederate banner, now historical.

clue.text: Person in van warning old policeman

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
a Bow Street Runner was an early London police officer

explanation.surface: Someone in a removal van warns a retired police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' looks like a vehicle, but it is short for vanguard, the front of a movement. Bow Street Runners were London's first police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in the vanguard goes ahead of others, like a herald or precursor.

clue.text: Not for immediate consumption in African country

definitions.meaning: takeaway food bought to eat elsewhere rather than on the premises
a nation in West Africa between Ghana and Benin

explanation.surface: Takeaway food in a West African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Food bought to take away is not eaten there and then, and the West African republic carries the same name.

clue.text: Official has right to wear singular fabric

indicators.note: the word for singular puts on the right abbreviation like a garment, so it goes inside

parts.note: singular means one alone
cord is corded fabric such as corduroy

explanation.surface: An official is entitled to wear a unique cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wear' makes the right sign worn inside the word for singular, as a body sits inside clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something formally recorded is stated publicly, so it is official.

clue.text: Ambitious type is on time after rush

indicators.note: after means the rest of the wordplay comes behind the word for rush
in a down clue, on means placed above, so the time abbreviation sits below

parts.note: to career is to rush along headlong

explanation.surface: A go-getter is punctual after rushing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mainly concerned with personal advancement at work is ambitious.

clue.text: Casually boast of title to renounce

parts.note: a title is the name of a book or work
to drop a claim is to renounce it

explanation.surface: Someone casually brags about a title they are giving up.
explanation.definitionFit: Mentioning famous acquaintances offhandedly is a way of showing off in passing.

clue.text: Bloody, having entered a royal conflict — getting away from the front

indicators.note: having entered means the following pieces go inside the word for bloody

parts.note: something bloody is red with blood
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A bloody figure, involved in a royal war, flees the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting away from the front' reads as fleeing a battle, but it simply means towards the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving towards the back means heading away from the front.

clue.text: As a libertine, be less than upright?

definitions.meaning: a dissolute man of loose morals
to slope or slant, as a stage does

explanation.surface: A dissolute man is not quite morally upright.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissolute pleasure-seeker is a rake, and to rake is to incline from the vertical.

clue.text: New driver from African country in part of Europe

indicators.note: from means the learner sign is taken away from the country

parts.note: Liberia is a country in West Africa
L stands for learner, the plate on a new driver's car

explanation.surface: A learner driver from West Africa arrives in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula holding Spain and Portugal is a region in the south-west of the continent.

clue.text: Astronomer's unreliable scheme making for confused discussion

parts.note: Edwin Hubble was an American astronomer
a bubble is a speculative scheme that bursts, like the South Sea Bubble

explanation.surface: A stargazer's dodgy plan leads to muddled talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a noisy babble of talk or general confusion.

clue.text: Reactionary type's feeble support for bishop

definitions.note: read as 'a reactionary type is', so the noun phrase matches

indicators.note: in a down clue, the support for a word goes beneath it

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
limp means weak and feeble

explanation.surface: A conservative figure gives the bishop only weak support.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp was a pompous reactionary cartoon character, and his name is used for any such person.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonel Blimp, the cartoon figure, became a byword for a pompous diehard conservative.

clue.text: Sort of voice one's given in ballot-box regularly

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of ballot-box is taken

explanation.surface: Everyone has a voice in the ballot box.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of 'ballot-box' gives the answer; 'voice' hints at a vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Alto is a singing range, the lowest female or highest male part.

clue.text: Not in favour of cutting caper

indicators.note: cutting means the last letter of the synonym for caper is chopped off

parts.note: an antic is a playful caper

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to cutting a prank short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' docks the final C of ANTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something is the same as opposing it.

clue.text: Divers from cutter getting expenses

parts.note: a razor is a blade that cuts
bills are expenses to be paid

explanation.surface: Divers are paid out of a cutter's expenses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' are birds: razorbills are auks that dive for fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Razorbills are seabirds that plunge underwater for fish, so they dive.

clue.text: Conclude how to prepare for winter walk

definitions.meaning: finish or bring to an end

definitions.text: how to prepare for winter walk
definitions.meaning: put on warm clothes before going out in the cold

explanation.surface: Finish with advice about dressing warmly for a cold stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish a meeting is to bring it to a close, and to dress warmly is to swaddle yourself.

clue.text: Getting money out of former partner by legal means

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a legal action is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Squeezing cash from an ex through the courts.
explanation.definitionFit: Extortion or demanding payment is the act of forcing money from someone.
